Look that you hedge your possession about with thornes, and binde up your siluer and gold:
And weigh your words in a ballance, and make a doore and barre for your mouth.
Beware you slide not by it, lest you fall before him that lieth in wait.
He that is mercifull, will lende to his neighbour, and he that strengthens his hande, keeps the Commandments.
Lend to your neighbour in time of his need, and pay you your neighbour again in due season.
Keep your word and deale faithfully with him, and you shall alwaies find the thing that is necessary for you.
Many when a thing was lent them, reckoned it to be found, and put them to trouble that helped them.

Until he has received, he will kisse a mans hand: and for his neighbours money he will speak submissely: but when he should repay, he will prolong the time, and returne words of griefe, and complaine of the time.

If he preuaile, he shall hardly receive the halfe, and he will count as if he had found it: if not; he has depriued him of his money, and he has gotten him an enemy without cause: he payeth him with cursings, and raylings: and for honor he will pay him disgrace.
Many therefore have refused to lend for other mens ill dealing, fearing to be defrauded.
Yet have you patience with a man in poor estate, and delay not to show him mercy.
Helpe the poor for the commandments sake, and turne him not away because of his pouertie.
Lose your money for your brother and your friend, and let it not rust under a stone to be lost.
Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the most high, and it shall do you bring more profite then golde.
Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliuer you from all affliction.
It shall fight for you against your enemies, better then a mighty shield and strong speare.
An honest man is suretie for his neighbour: but he that is impudent, will forsake him.
Forget not the friendship of your suretie: for he has given his life for you.
A sinner will ouerthrow the good estate of his suretie:
And he that is of an vnthankfull minde, will leave him in that deliuered him.
Suretiship has vndone many of good estate, and shaked them as a waue of the Sea: mighty men has it driuen from their houses, so that they wandred among strange nations.
A wicked man transgressing the commandments of the Lord, shall fall into suretiship: and he that undertakes and follows other mens businesse for gaine, shall fall into suits.
Helpe your neighbour according to your power, and beware that you your selfe fall not into the same.
The chiefe thing for life is water and bread, and clothing, and an house to couer shame.
Better is the life of a poor man in a meane cottage, then delicate fare in another mans house.
Be it little or much, holde you contented, that you hear not the reproch of your house.
For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where you are a stranger, you darest not open your mouth.
You shall entertaine and feast, and have no thankes: moreouer, you shall hear bitter words.
Come you stranger, and furnish a table, and feede me of that you have ready.
Give place you stranger to an honourable man, my brother comes to be lodged, and I have neede of mine house.
These things are grieuous to a man of understanding: the vpbraiding of house-roome, and reproching of the lender.
He that loves his son, causes him oft to feele the rodde, that he may have ioy of him in the end.
He that chastises his son, shall have ioy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.
He that teaches his son, grieves the enemie: and before his friends he shall rejoice of him.
Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he has left one behinde him that is like himselfe.
While he liued, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died he was not sorrowfull.
He left behinde him an auenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindnesse to his friends.
He that makes too much of his son, shall binde up his wounds, and his bowels will be troubled at every cry.
An horse not broken becomes headstrong: and a childe left to himselfe will be wilfull.
Cocker your childe, and he shall make you afraid: play with him, and he will do you bring to heauinesse.
Laugh not with him, lest you have sorrow with him, and lest you gnash your teeth in the end.
Give him no liberty in his youth, and winke not at his follies.
Bow downe his necke while he is young, and beate him on the sides while he is a childe, lest he waxe stubborne, and be disobedient to you, and so bring sorrow to your heart.
Chastise your son, and hold him to labor, lest his lewd behauiour be an offence to you.
Better is the poor being sound and strong of constitution, then a rich man that is afflicted in his body.
Health and good state of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth.
There is no riches above a sound body, and no ioy above the ioy of the heart.
Death is better then a bitter life, or continuall sickenesse.
Delicates powred upon a mouth shut up, are as dishes of food set upon a grave.
What good does the offering to an idole? for neither can it eat nor smell: so is he that is persecuted of the Lord.
He seeth with his eyes and groans, as an Eunuch that embraces a virgine, and sighs.
Give not over your mind to heauinesse, and afflict not your selfe in your own counsel.
The gladnesse of the heart is the life of man, and the ioyfulnes of a man prolongs his days.
Love your own soul, and comfort your heart, remoue sorrow far from you: for sorrow has killed many, and there is no profit therein.
Enuie and wrath shorten the life, and carefulnesse brings age before the time.
A cherefull and good heart will have care for his food and diet.
Watching for riches, consumes the flesh, and the care thereof drives away sleepe.
Watching care will not let a man slumber, as a sore disease breaks sleepe.
The rich has great labor in gathering riches together, and when he rests, he is filled with his delicates.
The poor labors in his poor estate, and when he leaves off, he is still needie.
He that loves gold shall not be iustified, and he that follows corruption, shall have enough thereof.
Gold has bin the ruine of many, and their destruction was present.
It is a stumbling block to them that sacrifice to it, and every foole shall be taken therewith.
Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold:
Who is he? and we will call him blessed: for wonderfull things has he done among his people.
Who has bene tried thereby, and found perfit? then let him glory. Who might offend and has not offended, or done evil, and has not done it?
His goods shall be established, and the congregation shall declare his alms.
If you sit at a bountifull table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much food on it.
Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked then an eye? therefore it weeps upon every occasion.
Stretch not your hand whithersoeuer it looks, and thrust it not with him into the dish.
Judge of your neighbour by your selfe: and be discreet in every point.
Eat as it becomes a man those things which are set before you: and deuoure not, lest you be hated.
Leave off first for manners sake, and be not vnsatiable, lest you offend.
When you sit among many, reach not your hand out first of all.
A very litle is sufficient for a man well nurtured, and he fetches not his wind short upon his bed.
Sound sleepe comes of moderate eating: he riseth early, and his wits are with him, but the paine of watching and choller, and pangs of the bellie are with an vnsatiable man.
And if you have bin forced to eat, arise, go forth, vomit, and you shall have rest.
My son, hear me, and despise me not, and at the last you shall find as I told you: in all your workes be quicke, so shall there no sickenesse come to you.
Who so is generous with his food, men shall speak well of him, and the report of his good housekeeping will be believed.
But against him that is a niggard of his food, the whole city shall murmure; and the testimonies of his niggardnesse shall not be doubted of.
Show not your valiantnesse in wine, for wine has destroyed many.
The furnace proves the edge by dipping: so does wine the hearts of the proud by drunkennesse.
Wine is as good as life to a man if it be drunke moderatly: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad.
Wine measurably drunke, and in season, brings gladnesse of the heart and cheerefulnesse of the minde.
But wine drunken with excesse, makes bitternesse of the minde, with brawling and quarreling.
Drunkennesse increases the rage of a foole until he offend, it diminishes strength, and makes wounds.
Rebuke not your neighbour at the wine, and despise him not in his mirth: give him no despitefull words, and presse not upon him with vrging him (to drinke.)
If you be made the master (of the feast) lift not your selfe up, but be among them as one of the rest, take diligent care for them, and so sit downe.
And when you have done all your office, take your place that you may be merry with them, and receive a crowne for your well ordering of the feast.
Do you speak that art the elder, for it becomes you, but with sound judgment, and hinder not musicke.
Power not out words where there is a musitian, and show not forth wisdom out of time.
A consort of musicke in a banket of wine, is as a signet of Carbuncle set in gold.
As a signet of an Emeraud set in a worke of gold, so is the melodie of musicke with pleasant wine.
Speak young man, if there be need of you: and yet scarsely when you are twise asked:
Let your speech be short, comprehending much in few words, be as one that knows, and yet holds his tongue.
If you be among great men, make not your selfe equall with them, and when ancient men are in place, use not many words.
Before the thunder goes lightening: and before a shamefast man shall go favor.
Rise up betimes, and be not the last: but get you home without delay.
There take your pastime, and do what you will: but sin not by proud speech
And for these things blesse him that made you, and has replenished you with his good things.
Who so fears the Lord, will receive his discipline, and they that seeke him early, shall find favor.
He that seeks the law, shall be filled therewith: but the hypocrite will be offended thereat.
They that fear the Lord shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.
A sinfull man will not be reproued, but finds an excuse according to his will.
A man of counsel will be considerate, but a strange and proud man is not daunted with fear, even when of himselfe he has done without counsel.
Do nothing without aduice, and when you have once done, repent not.
Go not in a way wherein you may fall, and stumble not among the stones.
Be not confident in a plaine way.
And beware of your own children.
In every good worke trust your own soul: for this is the keeping of the commandments.
He that believes in the Lord, takes heed to the commandment, and he that trusted in him, shall fare never the worse.
There shall no evil happen to him that fears the Lord, but in temptation even again he will deliuer him.
A wise man hateth not the Law, but he that is an hypocrite therein, is as a ship in a storme.
A man of understanding trusts in the Law, and the Law is faithfull to him, as an oracle.
Prepare what to say, and so you shall be heard, and binde up instruction, and then make answer.
The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheele: and his thoughts are like a rolling axeltree.
A stallion horse is as a mocking friend, he neighs under every one that sits upon him.
Why does one day excell another? when as all the light of every day in the year is of the Sunne.
By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.
Some of them has he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them has he made ordinary days.
And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.
In much knowledge the Lord has diuided them, and made their ways diverse.
Some of them has he blessed, and exalted, and some of them has he sanctified, and set neere himselfe: but some of them has he cursed, and brought low, and turned out of their places.
As the clay is in the potters hand to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.
Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.
So look upon all the workes of the most High, and there are two and two, one against another.
I awaked up last of all, as one that gathers after the grape-gatherers: by the blessing of the Lord I profited, and filled my wine-presse, like a gatherer of grapes.
Consider that I labored not for my selfe only, but for all them that seeke learning;
Hear me, O you great men of the people, and hearken with your eares you rulers of the Congregation:
Give not your son, and wife, your brother and friend power over you while you liuest, and give not your goods to another, lest it repent you: and you intreat for the same again.
As long as you liuest and have breath in you, give not your selfe over to any.
For better it is that your children should seeke to you, then that you shouldst stand to their courtesie.
In all your workes keep to your selfe the preheminence, leave not a staine in your honor.
At the time when you shall end your days, and finish your life, distribute your inheritance.
Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the asse: and bread, correction, and worke for a servant.
If you set your servant to labor, you shall find rest: but if you let him go idle, he shall seeke libertie.
A yoke and a collar do bow the necke: so are tortures and torments for an evil servant.
Sende him to labor that he be not idle: for idlenesse teaches much evil.
Set him to worke, as is fit for him; if he be not obedient, put on more heauy fetters.
But be not excessiue toward any, and without discretion do nothing.
If you have a servant, let him be to you as your selfe, because you have bought him with a price.
If you have a servant, intreate him as a brother: for you have neede of him, as of your own soul: if you intreate him evil, and he runne from you, which way will you go to seeke him?
The hopes of a man voyd of understanding are vaine, and false: and dreames lift up fooles.
Who so regards dreames, is like him that catches at a shadow, and follows after the winde.
The vision of dreames is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likenesse of a face to a face.
Of an unclean thing, what can be cleansed? and from that thing which is false, what truth can come?
Diuinations, and soothsayings, and dreames are vaine: and the heart fancies as a womans heart in trauell.
If they be not sent from the most high in your visitation, set not your heart upon them.
For dreames have deceiued many, and they have failed that put their trust in them.
The Law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithfull mouth.
A man that has trauailed knows many things: and he that has much experience, will declare wisdom.
He that has no experience, knows little: but he that has trauailed, is full of prudence.
When I trauailed, I saw many things: and I understand more, then I can expresse.
I was oft times in danger of death, yet I was deliuered because of these things.
The spirit of those that fear the Lord shall live, for their hope is in him that saueth them.
Who so fears the Lord, shall not fear nor be afraid, for he is his hope.
Blessed is the soul of him that fears the Lord: to whom does he look? and who is his strength?

For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection, and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a couer from the Sunne at noone, a preseruation from stumbling, and a helpe from falling.
He raises up the soul, and lightens the eyes: he gives health, life, and blessing.
He that sacrifices of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous, and the giftes of vniust men are not accepted.
The most high is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked, neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.
Who so brings an offering of the goods of the poor, does as one that kills the son before his fathers eyes.
The bread of the needie, is their life: he that defrauds him thereof, is a man of blood.
He that takes away his neighbours living, slays him: and he that defrauds the labourer of his hire, is a bloodshedder.
When one builds, and another pulls downe, what profite have they then but labor?
When one prays, and another curses, whose voice will the Lord hear?
He that washes himselfe after the touching of a dead body, if he touch it again, what avails his washing?
So is it with a man that fasts for his sins, and goes again and does the same: who will hear his prayer, or what does his humbling profit him?
He that keeps the law, brings offerings enow: he that takes heed to the commandment, offers a peace offering.
He that repays a good turne, offers fine floure: and he that gives alms, sacrifices praise.
To depart from wickednesse is a thing pleasing to the Lord: and to forsake vnrighteousnesse, is a propitiation.
You shall not appeare emptie before the Lord:
For all these things because of the commandment.
The offering of the righteous makes the Altar fat, and the sweete sauour thereof is before the most high.
The sacrifice of a just man is acceptable, and the memoriall thereof shall never be forgotten.
Give the Lord his honor with a good eye, and diminish not the first fruits of your hands.
In all your gifts show a cheerefull countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladnesse.
Give to the most high, according as he has enriched you, and as you have gotten, give with a cheerefull eye.
For the Lord recompenses, and will give you seven times as much.
Do not thinke to corrupt with gifts, for such he will not receive: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices, for the Lord is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.
He will not accept any person against a poor man: but will hear the prayer of the oppressed.
He will not despise the supplication of the fatherlesse: nor the widowe when she pours out her complaint.
Does not the teares run downe the widowes cheeks? and is not her crie against him that causes them to fall?
He that serves the Lord, shall be accepted with favor, and his prayer shall reach to the cloudes.
The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds: and until it come near he will not be comforted: and will not depart until the most High shall beholde to judge righteously, and execute judgment.

For the Lord will not be slacke, neither will the mighty be patient towards them, until he has smitten in sunder the loines of the vnmercifull, and repaid vengeance to the heathen: until he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the scepter of the unrighteous:
Until he have rendred to every man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their deuises, until he have iudged the cause of his people: and made them to rejoice in his mercy,
Mercy is seasonable in the time of affliction, as cloudes of raine in the time of drought.
Have mercy upon us, O Lord Alahayam of all, and behold us:
And send your fear upon all the nations that seeke not after you.
Lift up your hand against the strange nations, and let them see your power.
As you were sanctified in us before them: so be you magnified among them before us.
And let them do you know, as we have known you, that there is no Alahayam, but only you, O Alahayam.
Show new signes, and make other strange wonders: glorifie your hand and your right arm, that they may set forth your wonderous workes.
Raise up indignation, and power out wrath: take away the aduersarie and destroy the enemie.
Make the time short, remember the couenant, and let them declare your wonderfull works.
Let him that escapes, be consumed by the rage of the fire, and let them perish that oppresse the people.
Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we.
Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.
O Lord have mercy upon the people, that is called by your name, and upon Yahsharala, whom you have named your first borne.
O be mercifull to Jerusalem your holy city, the place of your rest.
Fill Sion with your vnspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory.
Give testimonie to those that you have possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have bin in your name.
Reward them that wait for you, and let your prophets be found faithfull.
O Lord hear the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron over your people, that all they which dwel upon the earth, may know that you are the Lord, the eternall Alahayam.
The belly devours all foods, yet is one food better than another.
As the palate tastes diverse kinds of venison: so does an heart of understanding false speeches.
A froward heart causes heauinesse: but a man of experience will recompense him.
A woman will receive every man, yet is one daughter better then another
The beautie of a woman cheers the countenance, and a man loves nothing better.
If there be kindnesse, meekenes, and comfort in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.
He that gets a wife, begins a possession, a helpe like to himselfe, and a pillar of rest.
Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled: and he that has no wife will wander up and downe mourning.
Who will trust a thiefe well appointed, that skips from city to city? so a man that has no house? and lodges wheresoeuer the night takes him?
Every friend saieth, I am his friend also: but there is a friend which is only a friend in name.
Is it not a griefe to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemie?
O wicked imagination, whence camest you in to couer the earth with deceit?
There is a companion, which rejoices in the prosperity of a friend: but in the time of trouble will be against him.
There is a companion which helps his friend for the belly, and takes up the buckler against the enemie.
Forget not your friend in your minde, and be not vnmindfull of him in your riches.
Every counseller extols counsel; but there is some that counsels for himselfe.
Beware of a counseller, and know before what neede he has (for he will counsel for himselfe) lest he cast the lot upon you:
And say to you, Your way is good: and afterward he stand on the other side, to see what shall befall you.
Consult not with one that suspects you: and hide your counsel from such as enuie you.

Neither consult with a woman touching her of whom she is iealous; neither with a coward in matters of war, nor with a merchant concerning exchange; nor with a buyer of selling; nor with an enuious man of thankfulnesse; nor with an vnmercifull man touching kindnesse; nor with the slouthfull for any worke; nor with an hireling for a year, of finishing worke; nor with an idle servant of much businesse: Hearken not to these in any matter of counsel.
But be continually with a godly man, whom you know to keep the commandments of the Lord, whose minde is according to your minde, and will sorrow with you, if you shall miscarry.
And let the counsel of your own heart stand: for there is no man more faithfull to you then it.
For a mans minde is sometimes inclined to tell him more then seven watchmen, that sit above in an high towre.
And above all this pray to the most high, that he will direct your way in truth.
Let reason go before every enterprise, and counsel before every action.
The countenance is a signe of changing of the heart.
Four manner of things appeare: good and evil, life and death: but the tongue ruleth over them continually.
There is one that is wise and teaches many, and yet is vnprofitable to himselfe.
There is one that shows wisdom in words, and is hated: he shall be destitute of all foode.
For grace is not given him from the Lord: because he is depriued of all wisdom.
Another is wise to himselfe: and the fruits of understanding are commendable in his mouth.
A wise man instructs his people, and the fruits of his understanding faile not.
A wise man shall be filled with blessing, and all they that see him, shall count him happy.
The days of the life of man may be numbred: but the days of Yahsharala are innumerable.
A wise man shall inherite glory among his people, and his name shalbe perpetuall.
My son prooue your soul in your life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that to it.
For all things are not profitable for all men, neither has every soul pleasure in every thing.
Be not vnsatiable in any dainty thing: nor too greedy upon foods.
For excesse of foods, brings sicknesse, and surfetting will turne into choler.
By surfetting have many perished, but he that takes heed, prolongs his life.
Honor a Phisitian with the honor due to him, for the vses which you may have of him: for the Lord has created him.
For of the most High comes healing, and he shall receive honor of the King.
The skill of the Phisitian shall lift up his head: and in the sight of great men he shalbe in admiration.
The Lord has created medicines out of the earth; and he that is wise will not abhorre them.
Was not the water made sweet with wood, that the vertue thereof might be known?
And he has given men skill, that he might be honored in his marueilous workes.
With such does he heale and takes away their paines.
Of such does the Apothecarie make a confection; and of his workes there is no end, and from him is peace over all the earth.
My son, in your sickenesse be not negligent: but pray to the Lord, and he will make you whole.
Leave off from sin, and order your hands aright, and cleanse your heart from all wickednesse.
Give a sweet sauour, and a memoriall of fine flowre: and make a fat offering, as not being.
Then give place to the phisitian, for the Lord has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.
There is a time when in their hands there is good successe.
For they shall also pray to the Lord, that he would prosper that, which they give, for ease and remedy to prolong life.
He that sins before his maker, let him fal into the hand of the Phisitian.
My son, let teares fall downe over the dead, and begin to lament, as if you had suffered great harme your selfe: and then couer his body according to the custome, and neglect not his buriall.
Weepe bitterly, and make great moane, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest you be evil spoken of: and then comfort your selfe for your heauinesse.
For of heauinesse comes death, and the heauinesse of the heart, breaks strength.
In affliction also sorrow remains: and the life of the poor, is the curse of the heart.
Take no heauines to heart: driue it away, and remember the last end.
Forget it not, for there is no turning again: you shall not do him good, but hurt your selfe.
Remember my judgment: for your also shall be so; yesterday for me, and to day for you.
When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest, and be comforted for him, when his spirit is departed from him.
The wisdom of a learned man comes by opportunitie of leasure: and he that has litle busines shall become wise.
How can he get wisdome that holds the plough, and that glories in the goad; that drives oxen, and is occupied in their labours, and whose talke is of bullocks?
He gives his minde to make furrowes: and is diligent to give the kine fodder.

So every carpenter, and workemaster, that labors night and day: and they that cut and graue seales, and are diligent to make great variety, and give themselues to counterfait imagerie, and watch to finish a worke.

The smith also sitting by the anuill, and considering the iron worke; the vapour of the fire wastes his flesh, and he fights with the heat of the furnace: the noise of the hammer and the anuill is ever in his eares, and his eies look still upon the patterne of the thing that he makes, he sets his mind to finish his worke, and watches to polish it perfitly.
So does the potter sitting at his worke, and turning the wheele about with his feet, who is alway carefully set at his worke: and makes all his worke by number.
He fashions the clay with his arm, and boweth downe his strength before his feet: he applies himselfe to lead it over; and he is diligent to make cleane the furnace.
All these trust to their hands: and every one is wise in his worke.
Without these cannot a city be inhabited: and they shall not dwell where they will, nor go up and downe.

They shall not be sought for in publike counsaile; nor sit high in the congregation: they shall not sit on the Judges seate, nor understand the sentence of judgment: they cannot declare justice, and judgment, and they shall not be found where parables are spoken.
But they will maintaine the state of the world, and their desire is in the worke of their craft.
But he that gives his minde to the Law of the most high, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seeke out the wisdome of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.
He will keep the sayings of the renowmed men: and where subtile parables are, he will be there also.
He will seeke out the secrets of graue sentences, and be conuersant in darke parables.
He shall serve among great men, and appeare before princes: he will travel through foreign countries, for he has tried the good, and the evil among men.
He will give his heart to resort early to the Lord that made him, and will pray before the most high, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.
When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall power out wise sentences, and give thankes to the Lord in his prayer.
He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.
He shall show foorth that which he has learned, and shall glory in the Law of the couenant of the Lord.
Many shall commend his understanding, and so long as the world endures, it shall not be blotted out, his memoriall shall not depart away, and his name shall live from generation to generation.
Nations shall shewe foorth his wisdom, and the congregation shall declare his praise.
If he die, he shall leave a greater name then a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.
Yet I have more to say which I have thought upon, for I am filled as the Moone at the full.
Hearken to me, you holy children, and budde foorth as a rose growing by the brooke of the field:
And give you a sweete sauour as frankincense, and flourish as a lilly, send foorth a smell, and sing a song of praise, blesse the Lord in all his workes.
Magnifie his Name, and shewe foorth his praise with the songs of your lips, and with harpes, and in praising him you shall say after this manner:
Al the works of the Lord are exceeding good, and whatever he commands, shalbe accomplished in due season.

And none may say, What is this? why is that? for at time conuenient they shall all be sought out: at his commandment the waters stood as an heape, and at the words of his mouth the receptacles of waters.
At his commandment is done whatever pleases him, and none can hinder when he will saue.
The workes of all flesh are before him, and nothing can be hid from his eyes.
He seeth from everlasting to everlasting, and there is nothing wonderfull before him.
A man neede not to say, What is this? why is that? for he has made all things for their vses.
His blessing couered the dry land as a riuer, and watered it as a flood.
As he has turned the waters into saltnesse: so shall the heathen inherite his wrath.
As his ways are plaine to the holy, so are they stumbling blockes to the wicked.
For the good, are good things created from the beginning: so evil things for sinners.
The principall things for the whole use of mans life, are water, fire, yron, and salt, floure of wheate, honie, milke, and the blood of the grape, and oyle, and clothing.
All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.
There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their furie lay on sore strokes, in the time of destruction they power out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.
Fire, and haile, and famine, and death: all these were created for vengeance:
Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword, punishing the wicked to destruction.
They shall reioice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth when neede is, and when their time is come, they shall not transgresse his word.
Therefore from the beginning I was resolued, and thought upon these things, and have left them in writing.
All the workes of the Lord are good: and he will give every needefull thing in due season.
So that a man cannot say, This is worse then that: for in time they shall all be well approued.
And therefore praise you the Lord with the whole heart and mouth, and blesse the Name of the Lord.
Great hardship is created for every man, and an heauy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mothers wombe, until the day that they returne to the mother of all things.
Their imagination of things to come, and the day of death their thoughts, and fear of heart:
From him that sits on a throne of glory, to him that is humbled in earth and ashes.
From him that wears purple, and a crown, to him that is clothed with a linnen frocke.
Wrath, and enuie, trouble and vnquietnesse, fear of death, and anger, and strife, and in the time of rest upon his bed, his night sleepe do change his knowledge.
A litle or nothing is his rest, and afterward he is in his sleepe, as in a day of keeping watch, troubled in the vision of his heart, as if he were escaped out of a battell:
When all is safe, he awakens, and marvels that the fear was nothing.
to all flesh, both man and beast, and that is seven fold more upon sinners.
Death and bloodshed, strife and sword, calamities, famine, tribulation, and the scourge:
These things are created for the wicked, and for their sakes came the flood.
All things that are of the earth shall turne to the earth again: and that which is of the waters does returne into the Sea.
All briberie and iniustice shall be blotted out: but true dealing shall endure for ever.
The goods of the vniust shall be dried up like a riuer, and shall vanish with noise, like a great thunder in raine.
While he opens his hand he shall rejoice: so shall transgressours come to nought.
The children of the ungodly shall not bring forth many branches: but are as unclean roots upon a hard rocke.
The weed growing upon every water, and banke of a riuer, shall be pulled up before all grasse.
Bountifulnes is as a most fruitfull garden, and mercifulnesse endures for ever.
To labor and to be content with that a man has, is a sweet life: but he that finds a treasure, is above them both.
Children and the building of a city continue a mans name: but a blamelesse wife is counted above them both.
Wine and musicke rejoice the heart: but the love of wisdom is above them both.
The pipe and the psalterie make sweet melodie: but a pleasant tongue is above them both.
Your eye desires favor and beautie: but more then both, corne while it is greene.
A friend and companion never meet amisse: but above both is a wife with her husband.
Brethren and helpe are against time of trouble: but alms shall deliuer more then them both.
Golde and siluer make the foote stand sure: but counsel is esteemed above them both.
Riches and strength lift up the heart: but the fear of the Lord is above them both: there is no want in the fear of the Lord, and it needs not to seeke helpe.
The fear of the Lord is a fruitfull garden, and covers him above all glory.
My son, lead not a beggers life: for better it is to die then to beg.
The life of him that depends on another mans table, is not to be counted for a life: for he pollutes himselfe with other mens food, but a wise man well nurtured will beware thereof.
Begging is sweet in the mouth of the shamelesse: but in his belly there shall burne a fire.

O death, how bitter is the remembrance of you to a man that lives at rest in his possessions, to the man that has nothing to vexe him, and that has prosperity in all things: yea to him that is yet able to receive food?
O death, acceptable is your sentence to the needy, and to him whose strength fails, that is now in the last age, and is vexed with all things, and to him that despairs and has lost patience.
Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before you, and that come after, for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.
And why art you against the pleasure of the most High? there is no inquisition in the graue, whether you have liued ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.
The children of sinners, are abhominable children: and they that are conuersant in the dwelling of the ungodly.
The inheritance of sinners children shall perish, and their posterity shall have a perpetuall reproch.
The children will complaine of an ungodly father, because they shall be reproched for his sake.
Woe be to you ungodly men which have forsaken the law of the most high Alahayam: for if you encrease, it shall be to your destruction.
And if you be borne, you shall be borne to a curse: and if you die, a curse shall be your portion.
All that are of the earth shall turne to earth again: so the ungodly shall go from a curse to destruction.
The mourning of men is about their bodies: but an ill name of sinners shall be blotted out.
Have regard to your name: for that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold.
A good life has but few days: but a good name endures for ever.
My children, keep discipline in peace: for wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seene, what profit is in them both?
A man that hideth his foolishnesse is better then a man that hideth his wisdom.
Therefore be shamefast according to my word: for it is not good to retaine all shamefastnesse, neither is it altogether approoued in every thing.
Be ashamed of whoredome before father and mother, and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man:
Of an offence before a judge and ruler, of iniquitie before a congregation and people, of vniust dealing before your partner and friend:
And of theft in regard of the place where you sojourn, and in regard of the truth of Alahayam and his couenant, and to leane with your elbow upon the food, and of scorning to give and take:
And of silence before them that salute you, and to look upon an harlot:
And to turne away your face from your kinsman, or to take away a portion or a gift, or to gaze upon another mans wife,
Or to be ouerbusie with his maide, and come not neere her bed, or of vpbraiding speaches before friends; and after you have given, vpbraide not:
Or of iterating and speaking again that which you have heard, and of reuealing of secrets.
So shall you be truely shamefast, and find favor before all men.
Of these things be not you ashamed, and accept no person to sin thereby.
Of the Law of the most High, and his Couenant, and of judgment to iustifie the ungodly:
Of reckoning with your partners, and traueilers: or of the gift of the heritage of friends:
Of exactnesse of ballance, and waights: or of getting much or little:
And of merchants indifferent selling, of much correction of children, and to make the side of an evil servant to bleed.
Sure keeping is good where an evil wife is, and shut up where many hands are.
Deliuer all things in number and waight, and put al in writing that you giuest out, or receive in.
Be not ashamed to informe the vnwise and foolish, and the extreeme aged that contends with those that are young, thus shall you be truely learned and approued of all men living.
The father waketh for the daughter when no man knows, and the care for her takes away sleepe; when she is young lest she pass away the flowre of her age, and being married, lest she should be hated:

In her virginitie lest she should be defiled, and gotten with childe in her fathers house; and having an husband, lest she should misbehaue herselfe: and when she is married, lest she should be barren.

Keep a sure watch over a shamelesse daughter, lest she make you a laughing stocke to your enemies, and a by-word in the city, and a reproch among the people, and make you ashamed before the multitude.
Behold not every bodies beauty, and sit not in the midst of women.
For from garments comes a moth, and from women wickednesse.
Better is the churlishnesse of a man, then a courteous woman, a woman I say, which brings shame and reproch.
I will now remember the works of the Lord, and declare the things that I have seene: in the words of the Lord are his workes.
The Sunne that gives light, looks upon all things: and the worke thereof is full of the glory of the Lord.
The Lord has not given power to the Saints to declare all his marueilous workes, which the Almightie Lord firmely setled, that whatever is, might be established for his glory.
He seeks out the deepe and the heart, and considers their crafty deuices: for the Lord knows all that may be known, and he beholds the signes of the world.
He declares the things that are past, and for to come, and reveals the steps of hidden things.
No thought escapes him, neither any word is hidden from him.
He has garnished the excellent workes of his wisdom, and he is from everlasting to everlasting, to him may nothing be added, neither can he be diminished, and he has no need of any counseller.
O how desireable are all his workes: and that a man may see even to a sparke.
All these things live and remain for ever, for all vses, and they are all obedient.
All things are double one against another: and he has made nothing vnperfit.
One thing establishes the good of another: and who shalbe filled with beholding his glory?
The pride of the height, the cleare firmament, the beautie of heaven, with his glorious show;
The Sunne when it appears, declaring at his rising, a marueilous instrument, the worke of the most High.
At noone it parches the country, and who can abide the burning heate thereof?
A man blowing a furnace is in works of heat, but the Sunne burns the mountaines three times more; breathing out fiery vapours, and sending foorth bright beames, it dims the eyes.
Great is the Lord that made it, and at his commandment it runs hastily.
He made the Moone also to serve in her season, for a declaration of times, and a signe of the world.
From the Moone is the signe of Feasts, a light that decreases in her perfection.
The moneth is called after her name, encreasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven,
The beautie of heaven, the glory of the starres, an ornament giving light in the highest places of the Lord.
At the commandment of the holy One, they will stand in their order, and never faint in their watches.
Look upon the rainebow, and praise him that made it, very beautifull it is in the brightnesse thereof.
It circles the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most high have bended it.
By his commandment he makes the snow to fall apace, and sends swiftly the lightnings of his iudgment.
Through this the treasures are opened, and clouds flie forth as foules.
By his great power he makes the cloudes firme, and the hailestones are broken small.
At his sight the mountaines are shaken, and at his will the South wind blows.

The noise of the thunder makes the earth to tremble: so does the Northren storme, and the whirlewinde: as birds flying he scatters the snow, and the falling downe thereof, is as the lighting of grashoppers.
The eye marvels at the beauty of the whitenesse thereof, and the heart is astonished at the raining of it.
The hoare frost also as salt he pours on the earth, and being congealed, it lieth on the toppe of sharpe stakes.
Wheu the colde North-winde blows, and the water is congealed into yce, it abides upon every gathering together of water, and clothes the water as with a brestplate.
It devours the mountaines, and burns the wildernesse, and consumes the grasse as fire.
A present remedy of all is a miste comming speedily: a dew comming after heate, refreshes.
By his counsel he appeases the deepe, and plants Ilands therein.
They that saile on the Sea, tell of the danger thereof, and when we hear it with our eares, we marueile thereat.
For therein be strange and wonderous workes, varietie of all kindes of beasts, and whales created.
By him the ende of them has prosperous successe, and by his word all things consist.
We may speak much, and yet come short: therefore in summe, he is all.
How shall we be able to magnifie him? for he is great above all his workes.
The Lord is terrible and very great, and marueilous is his power.
When you glorifie the Lord exalt him as much as you can: for even yet will he farre exceed, and when you exalt him, put foorth all your strength, and be not weary: for you can never go farre enough.
Who has seene him, that he might tell us? and who can magnifie him as he is?
There are yet hid greater things then these be, for we have seene but a few of his workes:
For the Lord has made all things, and to the godly has he given wisdom.
Let us now praise famous men, and our Fathers that begat us.
The Lord has wrought great glory by them, through his great power from the beginning.
Such as did beare rule in their kingdoms, men renowmed for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies:
Leaders of the people by their counsels, and learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent in their instructions.
Such as found out musical tunes, and reiected verses in writing.
Rich men furnished with abilitie, living peaceably in their habitations.
All these were honored in their generations, and were the glory of their times.
There be of them, that have left a name behind them, that their praises might be reported.
And some there be, which have no memorial, who are perished as though they had never bene, and are become as though they had never bene borne, and their children after them.
But these were mercifull men, whose righteousness has not been forgotten.
With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the couenant.
Their seed stands fast, and their children for their sakes.
Their seed shall remain for ever, and their glory shall not be blotted out.
Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives for evermore.
The people will tell of their wisdome, and the congregation will show forth their praise.
Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance, to all generations.
Noah was found perfect and righteous, in the time of wrath, he was taken in exchange (for the world) therefore was he left as a remnant to the earth, when the flood came.
An everlasting Couenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.
Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like to him:
Who kept the Law of the most High, and was in couenant with him, he established the Couenant in his flesh, and when he was proued, he was found faithfull.

Therefore he assured him by an othe, that he would blesse the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him, as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the starres, and cause them to inherit from Sea to Sea, and from the riuer to the vtmost part of the land.
With Isaac did he establish likewise the blessing of all men and the couenant,
And made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and diuided his portions, among the twelve tribes did he part them.
And he brought out of him a mercifull man, which found favor in the sight of all flesh, even Moses beloued of Alahayam and men, whose memoriall is blessed:
He made him like to the glorious Saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.
By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him a commandment for his people, and showed him part of his glory.
He sanctified him in his faithfulnesse, and meekenesse, and chose him out of all men.

He made him to hear his voyce, and brought him into the darke cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his Couenants, and Yahsharala his iudgments.
He exalted Aaron an holy man like to him, even his brother, of the tribe of Leui.
An everlasting couenant he made with him, and gave him the priesthood among the people, he beautified him with comely ornaments, and clothed him with a robe of glory.
He put upon him perfect glory: and strengthened him with rich garments, with breeches, with a long robe, and the Ephod:

And he compassed him with pomegranates, and with many golden bels round about, that as he went, there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the Temple, for a memoriall to the children of his people.
With an holy garment, with gold and blew silke, and purple the worke of the embroiderer; with a brestplate of judgment, and with Urim and Thummim.

With twisted scarlet, the worke of the cunning workeman, with precious stones grauen like seales, and set in gold, the worke of the Ieweller, with a writing engraued for a memoriall, after the number of the tribes of Yahsharala.
He set a crowne of gold upon the miter, wherein was engraued holinesse an ornament of honor, a costly worke, the desires of the eies goodly and beautiful.
Before him there were none such, neither did ever any stranger put them on, but only his children, and his childrens children perpetually.
Their sacrifices shall be wholy consumed every day twise continually.

Moises consecrated him, and anointed him with holy oile, this was appointed to him by an everlasting couenant, and to his seed so long as the heavens should remain, that they should minister to him, and execute the office of the priesthood, and blesse the people in his name.
He chose him out of all men living to offer sacrifices to the Lord, incense and a sweet sauour, for a memoriall, to make reconciliation for his people.
He gave to him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of iudgements, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and informe Yahsharala in his lawes.
Strangers conspired together against him, and maligned him in the wildernesse, even the men that were of Dathans, and Abirons side, and the congregation of Core with fury and wrath.
This the Lord saw and it displeased him, and in his wrathfull indignation, were they consumed: he did wonders upon them, to consume them with the fiery flame.
But he made Aaron more honourable, and gave him an heritage, and diuided to him the first fruits of the encrease, especially he prepared bread in abundance:
For they eat of the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and his seed:
Howbeit in the land of the people he had no inheritance, neither had he any portion among the people, for the Lord himselfe is his portion and inheritance.

The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeale in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart, when the people were turned backe, and made reconciliation for Yahsharala.

Therfore was there a couenant of peace made with him, that he should be the cheefe of the sanctuary, and of his people, and that he, and his posteritie should have the dignitie of the Priesthood for ever.

According to the couenant made with David son of Iesse, of the tribe of Judah, that the inheritance of the king should be to his posterity alone: so the inheritance of Aaron should also be to his seed.
Alahayam give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, that their good things be not abolished, and that their glory may endure for ever.

Joshua the son of Naue was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophesies, who according to his name was made great for the sauing of the elect of Alahayam, and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Yahsharala in their inheritance.
How great glory gat he when he did lift up his hands, and stretched out his sword against the cities?
Who before him so stood to it? for the Lord himselfe brought his enemies to him.
Did not the Sunne go backe by his meanes? and was not one day as long as two?
He called upon the most high Lord, when the enemies pressed upon him on every side, and the great Lord heard him.

And with hailestones of mighty power he made the battell to fall violently upon the nations, and in the descent (of Bethoron) he destroyed them that resisted, that the nations might know all their strength, because he fought in the sight of the Lord, and he followed the mighty one.
In the time of Moses also, he did a worke of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Iephunne, in that they withstood the Congregation, and withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring.
And of six hundred thousand people on foot, they two were preserued to bring them into the heritage, even to the land that flows with milk and hony.
The Lord gave strength also to Caleb, which remained with him to his old age, so that he entred upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage.
That all the children of Yahsharala might see that it is good to follow the Lord.
And concerning the Judges, every one by name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord, let their memory be blessed.
Let their bones flourish out of their place, and let the name of them that were honored, be continued upon their children.
Samuel the Prophet of the Lord, beloued of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.
By the Law of the Lord he iudged the Congregation, and the Lord had respect to Jacob.
By his faithfulnes he was found a true Prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithfull in vision.
He called upon the mighty Lord, when his enemies pressed upon him on every side, when he offered the sucking lambe.
And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard.
And he destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians, and all the princes of the Philistines.
And before his long sleepe he made protestations in the sight of the Lord, and his anoynted, I have not taken any mans goods, so much as a shoe, and no man did accuse him.
And after his death he prophesied, and showed the King his end, and lift up his voyce from the earth in prophesie, to blot out the wickednesse of the people.
And after him rose up Nathan to prophesie in the time of David.
As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Yahsharala.
He played with Lions as with kids, and with beares as with lambs.
Slew he not a gyant when he was yet but young? and did he not take away reproch from the people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat downe the boasting of Goliah?
For he called upon the most high Lord, and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warriour, and set up the horne of his people:
So the people honored him with ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in that he gave him a crowne of glory.
For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to nought the Philistines his aduersaries, and brake their horne in sunder to this day.
In all his workes he praised the holy one most High, with words of glory, with his whole heart he sung songs, and loued him that made him.
He set singers also before the Altar, that by their voyces they might make sweet melody, and daily sing praises in their songs.
He beautified their feasts, and set in order the solemne times, until the ende, that they might praise his holy Name, and that the Temple might sound from morning.
The Lord tooke away his sins, and exalted his horne for ever: he gave him a couenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yahsharala.
After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large.
Salomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honored; for Alahayam made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his Name, and prepare his Sanctuary for ever.
How wise were you in your youth, and as a flood filled with understanding.
Your soul couered the whole earth, and you filledst it with dark parables.
Your name went farre to the Ilands, and for your peace you were beloued.
The countreys marueiled at you for your Songs, and Prouerbs, and Parables, and interpretations.
By the Name of the Lord Alahayam, which is called the Lord Alahayam of Yahsharala, you did gather gold as tinne, and did multiply siluer as lead.
You did bow your loines to women, and by your body you were brought into subiection.
You dist staine your honor, and pollute your seed, so that you brought wrath upon your children, and were grieved for your folly.
So the kingdom was diuided, and out of Ephraim ruled a rebellious kingdom.

But the Lord will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his workes perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: therefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a roote to David.

Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seede he left behinde him Roboam, even the foolishnesse of the people, and one that had no understanding; who turned away the people through his counsel: there was also Ieroboam the son of Nabat, who caused Yahsharala to sin, and showed Ephraim the way of sin:
And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, that they were driuen out of the land.
For they sought out all wickednes, until the vengeance came upon them.
Then stood up Elias the Prophet as fire, and his word burnt like a lampe.
He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeale he diminished their number.
By the word of the Lord he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought downe fire.
O Elias, how were you honored in your wondrous deeds! and who may glory like to you!
Who did raise up a dead man from death, and his soul from the place of the dead by the word of the most Hie.
Who brought kings to destruction, and honourable men from their bedde.
Who heard the rebuke of the Lord in Sinai, and in Horeb the iudgment of vengeance.
Who anointed kings to take reuenge, and Prophets to succeed after him:
Who were taken up in a whirlewinde of fire, and in a charet of fierie horses:

Who were ordained for reproofes in their times, to pacifie the wrath of the Lordes judgment before it brake foorth into fury, and to turne the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love, for we shall surely live.
Elias it was, who was couered with a whirlewinde: and Elizeus was filled with his spirit: while he liued he was not mooued of any prince, neither could any bring him into subiection.
No word could overcome him, and after his death his body prophecied.
He did wonders in his life, and at his death were his works marueilous.

For all this the people repented not, neither departed they from their sins, until they were spoiled and caried out of their land, and were scattered through all the earth: yet there remained a small people, and a ruler in the house of David:
Of whom, some did that which was pleasing to Alahayam, and some multiplied sins.
Ezekias fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst thereof: he digged the hard rocke with yron, and made welles for waters.
In his time Sennacherib came up, and sent Rabsaces, and lift up his hand against Sion, and boasted proudly.
Then trembled their hearts and handes, and they were in paine as women in trauell.
But they called upon the Lord which is mercifull, and stretched out their hands towards him, and immediatly the holy One heard them out of heaven, and deliuered them by the ministery of Esay.
He smote the hoste of the Assyrians, and his Angel destroyed them.
For Ezekias had done the thing that pleased the Lord, and was strong in the ways of David his father, as Esay the Prophet, who was great and faithfull in his vision, had commanded him.
In his time the Sunne went backeward, and he lengthened the kings life.
He sawe by an excellent spirit what should come to pass at the last, and he comforted them that mourned in Sion.
He showed what should come to pass for ever, and secret things or ever they came.
The remembrance of Iosias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the arte of the Apothecarie: it is sweete as hony in all mouthes, and as musicke at a banquet of wine.
He behaued himselfe vprightly in the conuersion of the people, and tooke away the abominations of iniquitie.
He directed his heart to the Lord, and in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of Alahayam.
All, except David and Ezechias, and Iosias, were defectiue: for they forsooke the Law of the most High, (even) the kings of Iudah failed:
Therefore he gave their power to others, and their glory to a strange nation.
They burnt the chosen city of the Sanctuarie, and made the streets desolate according to the prophecie of Ieremias:
For they entreated him evil, who nevertheless was a prophet sanctified in his mothers wombe, that he might root out and afflict and destroy, and that he might build up also and plant.
It was Ezechiel who sawe the glorious vision, which was showed him upon the chariot of the Cherubims
For he made mention of the enemies under the raine, and directed them that went right.
And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Jacob, and deliuered them by assured hope.
How shall we magnifie Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand.
So was Jeshua the son of Iosedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy Temple to the Lord, which was prepared for everlasting glory.
And among the elect was Neemias whose renowme is great, who raised up for us, the walles that were fallen, and set up the gates and the barres, and raised up our ruines again.
But upon the earth was no man created like Enoch, for he was taken from the earth.
Neither was there a man borne like to Joseph, a gouernour of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord.
Sem and Seth were in great honor among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in the creation.
Simon the high priest the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the Temple:
And by him was built from the foundation the double height, the high fortresse of the wall about the Temple.
In his days the cisterne to receive water being in compasse as the sea, was couered with plates of brasse.
He tooke care of the Temple that it should not fall, and fortified the city against besieging.
How was he honored in the midst of the people, in his comming out of the Sanctuarie?
He was as the morning starre in the midst of a cloud: and as the moone at the full.
As the Sunne shining upon the Temple of the most High, and as the rainebow giving light in the bright cloudes.
And as the flowre of roses in the spring of the year, as lillies by the riuers of waters, and as the branches of the frankincense tree in the time of summer.
As fire and incense in the censer, and as a vessell of beaten gold set with all manner of precious stones,
And as a faire oliue tree budding forth fruit, and as a Cypresse tree which grows up to the cloudes.
When he put on the robe of honor, and was clothed with the perfection of glory, when he went up to the holy altar, he made the garment of holinesse honourable.

When he tooke the portions out of the priests hands, he himselfe stood by the hearth of the altar, compassed with his brethren round about, as a young cedar in Libanus, and as palme trees compassed they him round about.
So were all the sons of Aaron in their glory, and the oblations of the Lord in their hands, before all the congregation of Yahsharala.
And finishing the seruice at the altar, that he might adorne the offring of the most high Almighty,
He stretched out his hand to the cup, and powred of the blood of the grape, he powred out at the foote of the altar, a sweet smelling sauour to the most high King of all.
Then shouted the sons of Aaron, and sounded the siluer trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard, for a remembrance before the most High.
Then all the people together hasted, and fell downe to the earth upon their faces to worship their Lord Alahayam almighty the most High.
The singers also sang praises with their voices, with great variety of sounds was there made sweete melodie.
And the people besought the Lord the most High by prayer before him that is mercifull, until the solemnity of the Lord was ended, and they had finished his seruice.
Then he went downe, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Yahsharala, to give the blessing of the Lord with his lips, and to rejoice in his name.
And they bowed themselues downe to worship the second time, that they might receive a blessing from the most High.
Now therefore blesse you the Alahayam of all, which only does wonderous things every where, which exalts our days from the wombe, and deals with us according to his mercy.
He grant us ioyfulnesse of heart, and that peace may be in our days in Yahsharala for ever.
That he would confirme his mercy with us, and deliuer us at his time.
There be two manner of nations which my heart abhors, and the third is no nation.
They that sit upon the mountaine of Samaria, and they that dwell amongst the Philistines, and that foolish people that dwell in Sichem.
Yeshua the son of Sirach of Hierusalem has written in this book, the instruction of understanding and knowledge, who out of his heart powred forth wisdom.
Blessed is he that shall be exercised in these things, and he that layeth them up in his heart, shall become wise.
For if he do them, he shall be strong to all things, for the light of the Lord leads him, who gives wisdom to the godly: blessed be the Lord for ever. Amen. Amen.
I will thanke you, O Lord and king, and praise you O Alahayam my Sauiour, I do give praise to your name:

For you are my defeuder, and helper, and have preserued my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lippes that forge lies, and have been my helper against mine aduersaries.

And have deliuered me according to the multitude of your mercies, and greatnesse of your name, from the teeth of them that were ready to deuoure me, and out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the manifold afflictions which I had:
From the choking of fire on every side, and from the mids of the fire, which I kindled not:
From the depth of the belly of hel, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words.
By an accusation to the king from an unrighteous tongue, my soul drew neere even to death, my life was neere to the hell beneath:
They compassed me on every side, and there was no man to helpe me: I looked for the succour of men, but there was none:
Then thought I upon your mercy, O Lord, and upon your acts of old, how you deliver such as waite for you, and sauest them out of the hands of the enemies:
Then lifted I up my supplication from the earth, and prayed for deliuerance from death.
I called upon the Lord the father of my Lord, that he would not leave me in the days of my trouble, and in the time of the proud when there was no helpe.
I will praise your Name continually, and will sing praise with thankesgiuing, and so my prayer was heard:
For you sauedst me from destruction, and deliver me from the evil time: therefore will I give thankes and praise you, and blesse your Name, O Lord.
When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer.
I prayed for her before the Temple, and will seeke her out even to the end:
Even from the flowre until the grape was ripe, has my heart delighted in her, my foot went the right way, from my youth up sought I after her.
I bowed downe mine eare a litle and received her, and gate much learning.
I profited therein, will I ascribe the glory to him that gives me wisdom:
For I purposed to do after her, and earnestly I followed that which is good, so shall I not be confounded:
My soul has wrestled with her, and in my doings I was exact, I stretched foorth my hands to the heaven above, and bewailed my ignorances of her.
I directed my soul to her, and I found her in purenesse, I have had my heart ioyned with her from the beginning, therefore shall I not be forsaken.
My heart was troubled in seeking her: therefore have I gotten a good possession.
The Lord has given me a tongue for my reward, and I will praise him therewith.
Draw neere to me you vnlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.
Why are you slow, and what say you of these things, seeing your souls are very thirstie?
I opened my mouth, and said, buy her for your selues without money.
Put your necke under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction, she is hard at hand to find.
Behold with your eies, how that I have had but little labor, and have gotten to me much rest.
Get learning with a great summe of money, and get much gold by her.
Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and be not ashamed of his praise.
Worke your worke betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.
